svg.text: Why the continuation stalls along the weak directions
One Newton step along a weak direction (a model, not data)
Same start and slope, two curvatures. Newton jumps to where its straight line reaches zero; along a weak direction that is far (slope σ small), and the curve has bent back up by then.
distance along the weak direction (units of F₀/σ)
residual (units of F₀)

g.title: converges: k = c·F₀/σ² = 0.3: Newton lands at F = 0.15 F₀
stalls: k = 2.5: Newton lands at F = 1.25 F₀
the zero of Newton's straight line, t = F₀/σ

svg.text: Newton's line reaches zero at t = F₀/σ
k = 2.5: lands at 1.25 F₀, above its start
line search ends at the lowest point, 0.8 F₀: the stall
Newton's straight line
stalls: k = 2.5
converges: k = c·F₀/σ² = 0.3
pinned + one full step, T73
deflated Newton, to T48
The symptom: the step in D collapses where Newton stops converging
Each point is the distance from a converged point to its run's previous one. After a failed solve the step halves, so a stall shows as a dive; each fix let the steps recover.
dimension D
step in D (log scale)
